recognize_zh: 服用奎寧類藥物 (chloroquine) 的病人周邊血中，白血球細胞質出現不尋常的顆粒：A 為帶空泡與細小紫紅色顆粒的單核樣細胞，B 為細胞質佈滿粗大深紫色顆粒的分葉核嗜中性球，需結合用藥史判讀。
features: Panel A: mononuclear cell with large kidney-shaped nucleus and moderately condensed chromatin
Panel A: pale grey-blue cytoplasm with multiple small clear vacuoles and scattered fine red-purple granules
Panel B: segmented neutrophil (three lobes joined by thin filaments)
Panel B: cytoplasm densely filled with coarse, dark purple granules, heavier than normal neutrophilic granulation
Background red cells normochromic without obvious inclusions
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows leukocytes with abnormal cytoplasmic contents. One mononuclear (monocytoid) cell contains a folded nucleus and vacuolated cytoplasm with scattered fine azurophilic granules, and a segmented neutrophil shows coarse, dark, toxic-appearing cytoplasmic granulation. The red cells are unremarkable. In the clinical context of chloroquine therapy, these cytoplasmic changes are consistent with a drug-associated leukocyte granulation/vacuolation artifact; infection-related toxic change and inherited granulation anomalies should be excluded clinically.

ddx.vs: Toxic change is usually accompanied by Döhle bodies, left shift and clinical infection, whereas the drug effect occurs without sepsis and resolves on drug withdrawal.
Alder-Reilly granules are coarse and present in all granulocytes, lymphocytes and monocytes constitutively in mucopolysaccharidoses, not acquired in relation to a drug.
Chédiak-Higashi shows few giant fused granules rather than numerous uniform coarse granules.
